text: Reify has no rustfmt gate: no rustfmt.toml exists and neither `scripts/verify.sh` nor `hooks/pre-commit` invokes `cargo fmt`/rustfmt — verify.sh's lint pass is only `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

The reify codebase is intentionally not rustfmt-clean under its pinned toolchain (rustc 1.96.0 / rustfmt 1.9.0-stable, edition 2024 per the workspace Cargo.toml): it is a hand-maintained house style that deliberately diverges from rustfmt defaults, not an oversight.

With no rustfmt.toml in the reify tree, rustfmt's default `use_small_heuristics` chain-width of 60 disagrees with the hand-written style in many files; the tree carried roughly 165 pre-existing `cargo fmt --check` diffs under the pinned 1.96.0 toolchain as of 2026-07-26.

Per-crate rustfmt drift census for reify: reify-stdlib ~946 diffs, reify-audit ~728KB of diff, reify-eval 149 files / ~37k lines, reify-compiler ~150 (base commit aa858e10a9), reify-constraints ~90. Each figure is a dated point measurement; re-derive with `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check` before relying on it.

Do not run `cargo fmt`, `cargo fmt -p <crate>`, or `cargo fmt --all` for a targeted fix in reify: it reformats the entire crate/file (observed up to 149 files / ~37k lines) even when only one function needed a change, producing massive unrelated churn.

A red `cargo fmt --check` in reify is a pre-existing repo-wide condition, not a regression you introduced. To decide whether a flagged violation is actually yours, confirm the flagged construct is absent from `git diff <base>..HEAD`, since line numbers shift when you add lines above pre-existing violations.

To check your own reify edits for new drift, prefer `cargo fmt -p <crate> -- --check`, which auto-reads edition 2024 from Cargo.toml. Flag order matters: `cargo fmt --check -p <crate>` has been observed to non-deterministically error `Unrecognized option: 'p'`.

To format only your own new or edited files in reify, invoke rustfmt directly on those paths with `rustfmt --edition 2024 <paths...>` instead of `cargo fmt -p <crate>`, which would reformat large amounts of unrelated code.

Because reify's real gate is `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (scripts/verify.sh:2010-2012), rustc lints like `dead_code` are hard errors: an unused `pub(crate)` helper or struct field added ahead of the step that consumes it needs a targeted `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a comment.

The reify-gui debug MCP is driven by POSTing JSON-RPC to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp` — the `/mcp` path, not the bare host:port. The route is defined in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs as `.route("/mcp", post(handle_mcp))`.

The reify-gui debug port is per-worktree, not a fixed singleton: `scripts/setup-worktree-debug-port.sh` resolves it once, writes it to both `.mcp.json` and stdout, and `git update-index --skip-worktree`s .mcp.json. Server-side `resolve_debug_port()` in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs reads `REIFY_DEBUG_PORT`, defaulting to 3939.

Entries written 2026-06-04 claimed the reify-debug server binds a fixed singleton 127.0.0.1:3939 that cannot be redirected, so a worktree could not run a GUI acceptance unless it owned :3939 and should escalate infra_issue. That gap is closed by tasks 4340 and 4345 (both DONE, verified 2026-07-27) — provision your own port instead of parking.

Plain curl drives the reify-debug MCP: send headers `Content-Type: application/json` AND `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream` (omitting text/event-stream fails), with body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":N,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"<tool>","arguments":{...}}}`. No initialize handshake and no Mcp-Session-Id header are needed — stateless POSTs work (verified 2026-07-22).

Raw curl is the only route to the reify-debug MCP when the `mcp__reify-debug__*` tools are not registered in the agent session: the session's .mcp.json entry binds only if the port was already listening at session start, so a GUI launched mid-session never registers.

reify-debug MCP results need a double decode: `result.content[0].text` is itself a JSON string needing a second parse. For the `screenshot` tool the image arrives as `result.content[0].data`, a base64 PNG to decode to a file and Read.

The best reify-debug MCP render assertion is `store_state` → `viewports["design-main"].meshCount` for how many bodies actually render; `mesh_stats` lists every mesh the engine emitted with entity_path, so comparing it against meshCount proves hidden != absent. Use `tools/list` to discover live schemas rather than trusting a written inventory.

To launch a second reify-gui instance without a build, reuse an existing built binary and the already-running vite (port 1420 serves any instance): `cd /home/leo/src/warm-lanes/personal/gui-dev && setsid nohup env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/reify-deps/lib REIFY_DEBUG=1 REIFY_DEBUG_PORT=<free port> target/debug/reify-gui <absolute .ri path>`. A fresh dev GUI instead uses `REIFY_DEBUG=1 REIFY_DEBUG_PORT=<free port> scripts/run-gui-dev.sh <file.ri>`.

`open_file{path}` plus `wait_for_idle` loads a different example into an already-running reify-gui, so checking N examples costs one build rather than N. A cold debug build with feature `gui` took ~25 min in a warm lane, so launch it detached early and poll while doing other verification.

For a reify-gui acceptance gate, prefer the H0 e2e harness on a free port over the agent's own reify-debug MCP client, driving it via the `rpc<T>()` JSON-RPC envelope in gui/test/visual/run.ts. Value-assertion scenarios live in gui/test/visual/assertions.ts (VALUE_SCENARIOS) and run via `npm run test:e2e`, which is NOT CI-gated (no .github/workflows, per the reify-debug-mcp-expansion PRD §5).
In reify, PRD and docs artifacts must be committed DIRECTLY on main in project_root (/home/leo/src/reify). Do not route docs through the orchestrator merge queue and do not use scripts/land.sh.

Both branch-based landing paths are slow for docs in reify: the merge gate stamps DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge, forcing scripts/verify.sh to --scope all (contract C2) and --profile both, and dark-factory's INV-1 (task 2883) refuses the docs-only trivial pass at merge role and escalates to the full global gate.

A plain commit on reify's main runs hooks/pre-commit -> `verify.sh all --profile debug --scope staged --include-infra` with DF_VERIFY_ROLE unset, and decide_scope classifies `docs/*|*.md|*.yaml|*.yml` as no-heavy-checks, so a docs-only staged set yields an empty plan ("verify.sh: nothing to verify") and exits 0 in seconds.

A hook-gated commit on reify's main is sanctioned, not a violation: hooks/pre-commit runs project-checks and then calls main_gate_mark, so hooks/reference-transaction logs the ref move as SANCTIONED. CLAUDE.md's main-gate invariant only forbids moving main WITHOUT a gate.

The reify docs-landing SOP covers PRD .md, capability-manifest .md, and the YAML sidecar, but NOT .ri fixtures under tests/prd-gate/fixtures/: decide_scope's docs fast path does not match `tests/prd-gate/fixtures/*.ri`, so staging those escalates pre-commit to the full ~20k-test workspace nextest run (45+ min).

The .ri-fixture escalation was observed three times: 2026-07-02 (killed at the 2-min tool timeout mid-clippy, exit 143, commit did not land) and twice on 2026-07-25 (the stdlib-namespace manifest landing with 6 fixtures, and the constrained-2d-sketch landing rejected by two load-flaked reify-audit PTODO CLI tests). Tracking task is reify #5536.

The reify docs-landing sequence is: write artifacts as untracked files at their canonical paths; file the batch with planning_mode=True, wire deps, then commit_planning (which stamps the on-disk sidecar in place); `git add <each exact file path>`; then `git commit --only <same exact paths> -F <msgfile>`. Never land an unstamped sidecar and stamp afterwards.

When committing docs in reify's project_root, never use `git add -A`, `git add .`, or a directory add — project_root is a shared hot checkout with concurrent /prd sessions and the orchestrator, so a directory add sweeps foreign untracked files into your commit. Use `--only` with an explicit pathspec to ignore foreign staged state.

Two git gotchas when landing reify docs: `git commit --only -- <path>` cannot commit an untracked path ("did not match any file(s) known to git"), so new files must be `git add`-ed first; and `-F <msgfile>` must come BEFORE any `--` pathspec separator or git parses the message file as a pathspec ("outside repository").

In reify, `git commit --no-verify` alone on main is fatal — `reify.mainGate.enforce` is true, so no sentinel is marked and hooks/reference-transaction hard-aborts the unsanctioned main move. An older 2026-05-27 entry called `--no-verify` on main "the vetted-safe path when contained" for doc-only changes; that guidance is prohibited.

`REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS=1` is a genuine code-recognised break-glass path: hooks/reference-transaction's `main_gate_bypass_on` check runs at :82 before the sentinel check at :118 and unconditionally allows and logs the move. It only stops the ref-move abort — the verify gate still does not run and no sentinel is marked, so it is not an everyday path.

For new/untracked files under break-glass in reify, use the private-index procedure: `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<scratch> git read-tree HEAD`, `git add ...`, then `REIFY_MAIN_GATE_BYPASS=1 git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null commit --no-verify`, inside a capture-HEAD-before / recheck-before-commit retry loop.

After a private-index commit lands in reify, the shared index is stale for exactly the committed paths — `git status` shows them as staged `D` plus untracked, and a sibling session could sweep deletions of the just-landed files. Immediately run `git reset -q -- <those files>` and confirm `git status --porcelain -- <files>` is clean; applied for evidence commit ba7bbcfb53 (26 files).

For a high-contention landing on reify's main, use an atomic CAS instead of `git commit`: capture X=$(git rev-parse refs/heads/main), build the tree from X with the one file replaced, `git commit-tree`, then `git update-ref refs/heads/main NEW X` (retry from the new X if main moved), and finally `git reset -q`. Used 2026-05-31 to land commit 8de0eb13d2 on attempt 1.

PRD markdown must be committed to reify's main BEFORE its batch is flipped for dispatch, because task workers branch from main and need the PRD on disk. The full flip is: commit PRDs, then bulk `set_task_status(ids, "pending")` (comma-separated handles ~120 ids in one call), then restart the orchestrator if it was stopped.

Never run `git checkout -b` in reify's project_root — it moves the running orchestrator's checkout off main. Confirm HEAD == main before committing, since the offline lane can leave project_root on another branch, and pass a Bash timeout >= 300000 because pre-commit can exceed the default 2-minute tool timeout.

A 2026-06-19 entry claimed a docs-only diff submitted to reify's merge queue takes the worker's trivial-pass fast path and returns done within a bounded wait. That premise was falsified twice, including a direct 2026-07-24 observation of a docs-only PRD submission running the full ~20k-test post-merge verify.

`merge_request` accepts a NON-numeric task_id (a descriptive slug works), its `branch` argument must omit the `task/` prefix because the worker prepends it, and `worktree` may be the main checkout since the worker merges in its own _merge-verify worktree.

Cost evidence for the docs-landing SOP: on 2026-07-25 the resolution-unification and stdlib-namespace PRD .md files landed via `Merge task/task/prd/...` branches through the merge queue while their capability-manifest .md and .yaml halves were left stranded untracked in project_root — splitting one artifact across two vehicles lost half of it.

A memory consolidation claiming "all earlier entries are deleted" must enumerate the deleted ids AND re-run the discovery query afterwards to prove the set is closed. The docs-prd-landing cluster failed that four times; discover it deterministically via get_memories_by_metadata(project_id='reify', filters={'topic': 'docs-prd-landing'}), never by semantic ranking.

In reify, before remediating a harness-layout gate failure for a new top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs`, run `grep -c '^crates/<crate>/' tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest`: count 0 means move the file into a harness; count > 0 means a grandfather row addition is legitimate.

The reify harness-layout gate fires when a diff adds a new top-level `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs` in one of the 5 consolidatable crates (reify-cli, reify-syntax, reify-kernel-occt, reify-eval, reify-compiler), turning `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh --from-git` red with `reason=unregistered-standalone` or `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` red with `reason=unsanctioned-standalone`, even though the test compiles and passes.

When a reify crate's row count in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest is 0, its consolidation leaf has landed and adding a baseline row is FORBIDDEN because it un-ratchets a finished consolidation; the manifest header calls itself "a RATCHET, NOT A PERMANENT ALLOW-LIST" and PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md §5 C2(b) requires that "no new gratuitous standalone binary re-accretes".

The reify diff-scoped gate `scripts/check-harness-baseline-registration.sh` inspects only TOP-LEVEL `crates/<c>/tests/*.rs` — its `harness_layout_in_scope_standalone` check rejects anything nested below tests/ — so `git mv`ing the file into `tests/harness_<sub>/<f>.rs` takes it out of scope and the gate goes green with no manifest edit at all.

For a reify crate still grandfathered (baseline row count > 0), adding `crates/<crate>/tests/<file>.rs` to tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest in the SAME diff, in ambient-locale `sort` order, is a legitimate "conscious row addition" sanctioning mechanism — but folding the test into an existing subsystem harness is still preferred, and the row addition should be reserved for a crate with no harness unit yet.

Two categories of reify test file skip the harness-layout gate entirely: `harness_*.rs` files (governed by the 20000-line kLOC cap instead) and the 7 override binaries. The manifest header's per-crate and total counts are a frozen base-commit snapshot, deliberately stale against the live file, and must never be edited.

The reify per-crate harness census is volatile and no dated snapshot should be trusted: a prior canonical asserted reify-compiler had ZERO `harness_*.rs` files on 2026-07-24, but four (harness_langcore, harness_patterns, harness_traits, harness_auto_binding) landed overnight via task 5283 in merged commit 0360b1c25fc105c2dbb6fc9bc62dde78dbb596f4, falsifying it by 2026-07-25.

The reify anti-re-accretion guard `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` (PRD merge-gate-compile-cost.md W1, task 5265 leaf B1) reads the checked-in grandfather baseline `tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest`, created at 867 rows (reify-cli 73, reify-syntax 61, reify-kernel-occt 48, reify-eval 395, reify-compiler 290, excluding the 2 in-scope overrides tensegrity_t0a and representation_within_assertion).

The reify kLOC-cap guard `tests/infra/test_harness_kloc_cap.sh` is classified `pool` in run-all-classification.manifest and runs in the merge-tier run_all suite on every merge_request; its rule (b) sanctions a top-level `crates/<c>/tests/*.rs` iff it is `harness_*.rs`, one of the 7 override binaries, or listed in the baseline.

Anyone writing a reify consolidation leaf must delete the moved files' rows from tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest IN THE SAME DIFF when relocating former `tests/<file>.rs` into `tests/harness_<sub>/<file>.rs`; the baseline ratchets DOWN and empty means fully consolidated. Skipping it leaves the guard either falsely green or red on a genuinely new stray.
In reify, `CompiledModule.functions` is USER-SOURCE-ONLY: `compile_source_with_stdlib` does NOT put stdlib/prelude `pub fn` bodies into it.

`crates/reify-compiler/src/compile_builder/functions_phase.rs` builds a separate list for compile-time overload dispatch via `ctx.resolution_functions = merge_prelude_functions(&ctx.functions, &prelude_fns)`, under an in-source comment stating "`ctx.functions` (user-only) remains the output stored in CompiledModule". That comment lives in functions_phase.rs, not in ctx.rs, which earlier entries mis-attributed.

In reify-compiler, `ctx.functions` is what gets moved into the built `CompiledModule { .., functions: self.functions, .. }` in compile_builder/ctx.rs, while `resolution_functions` is used for resolution only and then discarded. Cite the symbols (functions_phase's prelude-merge block and `Ctx::into_compiled_module`) rather than line numbers, which drift.

The probe establishing that reify's `CompiledModule.functions` is user-source-only: a fixture with zero user `fn` items compiles with 0 Error diagnostics and `module.functions.len() == 0` (measured 2026-07-26 under task 5410).

A reify test using `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)` has a function table empty of prelude fns, so no stdlib `.ri` body ever executes; on a lookup miss `eval_user_function_call` returns `Value::Undef` (crates/reify-expr/src/lib.rs ~:1625).

Under the `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)` harness, a name+arity intercept in reify-expr `eval_expr` cannot be "beaten" by a stdlib `.ri` body: removing the intercept yields `Value::Undef`, never the `.ri` placeholder's value. A test asserting `Value::Undef` is therefore a no-op guard, and a fixture discriminates iff the intercept's expected value is NOT `Undef`.

The user-source-only finding invalidated the "placeholder .ri body would return X" framing in crates/reify-expr/tests/option_recovery_eval_tests.rs, including the "coincidentally correct" note at ~:575-584, and in the task-5410 drift-guard doc comments.

The reify production path differs from the compiler test harness: `reify_eval::merge_functions` (crates/reify-eval/src/lib.rs ~:1425, `pub(crate)`) unconditionally appends prelude fns into the runtime dispatch table, so any test that needs a `.ri` body to actually shadow or compete must go through reify-eval (Engine / merge_functions), not `EvalContext::new(&values, &module.functions)`.

There is a capability gap in reify's compiler API: `reify_compiler::merge_prelude_functions` (crates/reify-compiler/src/lib.rs ~:332) is `pub`, but no public accessor exposes the compiled prelude's `CompiledFunction` slice to feed it, so an out-of-crate caller cannot reconstruct the production function table from the compiler API alone.

The reify C1 harness move is `git mv crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs crates/<c>/tests/harness_<sub>/<f>.rs`, then declaring it in `tests/harness_<sub>.rs` with `#[path = "harness_<sub>/<f>.rs"] mod <f>;`. The explicit `#[path]` is MANDATORY — a bare `mod <f>;` at an integration-test crate root resolves to the sibling `tests/<f>.rs`, not the subdir.

The reify C1 harness move preserves test selection: it prefixes every test's nextest name with `<f>::`, so `test(/^<f>::/)` selects exactly that former binary's tests. Consolidation is selection-neutral because no `.config/nextest.toml` or tests/infra filterset references reify-eval test files by name — only the 7 override binaries use `binary()`.

When a reify test file moves one directory deeper into `tests/harness_<sub>/`, source-relative `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` paths need exactly one extra `../` (fixtures/ becomes ../fixtures/; ../../../examples/ becomes ../../../../examples/), while `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), ...)` loads are move-safe and must NOT be touched. A successful `cargo nextest list -p <crate>` already proves include-path correctness because `include_str!` resolves at compile time.

After a reify C1 harness move, a shared `tests/common/mod.rs` helper referenced via bare `mod common;` breaks because the bare declaration now resolves relative to the new subdir (`harness_<sub>/<f>/common.rs`). Fix it with `#[path = "../common/mod.rs"] mod common;`, relative to the submodule's new directory; precedent is crates/reify-eval/tests/harness_geometry.rs.

A reify test file that is `include!()`d from a src `#[cfg(test)]` block must NOT be moved during harness consolidation because moving it breaks the src-side include — copy it in place instead. Example: crates/reify-eval/src/compute_targets/elastic_static.rs `include!`s tests/as_printed_zones_test_fixtures.rs.

Any reify test file installing a process-wide `#[global_allocator]` (e.g. common::alloc_counter::CountingAllocator) must stay top-level AND grandfathered in tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest: two in one binary is a "multiple global allocators" compile error, and one shared allocator corrupts sibling alloc-count deltas.

The most commonly forgotten step of a reify harness move is the ratchet: remove each moved file's `crates/<c>/tests/<f>.rs` row from tests/infra/harness-layout-baseline.manifest in the SAME commit as the move.

Two reify harness-move non-issues: crate-level `#![allow(...)]` inner attributes remain valid as module inner attributes after the move with no change needed, and reify-eval's Cargo.toml auto-discovers tests (0 explicit `[[test]]` entries), so no Cargo.toml edit is needed when adding or moving harness files.

Alternating `cargo nextest list --workspace` and `cargo nextest list -p <crate>` triggers full ~7-minute recompiles because feature unification differs between the two invocations; pick ONE invocation form and stick to it for the whole session.

The proof obligation for a layout-only reify harness change is that the BT-1 total `#[test]`-fn count is UNCHANGED (reify-eval was 4690 at the time of task #5278). Worked example of a clean move, task #5342 commit 894377054c: two new helix-sweep tests moved with 0 content bytes changed, gate PASS added=2 violations=0, kloc-cap 16/16, clippy 0 warnings.

Cargo decides whether to re-run a build script by comparing each `cargo:rerun-if-changed` path's mtime against the mtime of `target/<profile>/build/<pkg>-<hash>/output` — strict `>`, at nanosecond resolution. That `output` file, not a separate timestamp file, is the freshness reference.

Anything that bumps a cargo build-script `output` file's mtime silently suppresses the rerun and links the previously compiled artifact with no warning. Verified empirically 2026-07-27 with a throwaway crate: change a watched file then `touch` its `output` 5 s newer and the build script does not run; restore `output` 5 s older and it runs.

Warm-lane seeding defeats `cargo:rerun-if-changed` for tracked files: scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh bulk-stamps every non-`target/` file to 2020-01-01 (the D5 mtime-normalization block) while `target/` is reflinked with `cp -a` preserving base mtimes, so a 2020-stamped tracked file can never exceed a 2026-dated `output` and the base's compiled artifact is linked verbatim.

The warm-lane rerun-if-changed inversion was measured in _lane-37 on 2026-07-27: tree-sitter-reify/grammar.js stamped 2020-01-01 against four target/debug/build/tree-sitter-reify-*/output files at 2026-07-27 01:14. Context is task #5629 / esc-5392-1, audited across cc-based build scripts by task #5630.

The `_touch_git_delta` rescue in scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh re-touches only tracked files differing from EFFECTIVE_BASE_COMMIT and is skipped entirely when that resolves empty, making it a conditional mitigation rather than a guarantee. The dangerous direction of the exposure is a false green, where a C/C++ or grammar change is verified against the previously compiled object.

The claim that scripts/seed-warm-lane.sh's `sed -i` relocation sweep bumps build-script `output` files to seed-time is superseded: task 5630 made the links-metadata/OUT_DIR relocation sweep mtime-preserving, capturing `stat -c '%y'` before the `sed -i` and restoring it with GNU `touch -d` afterwards at full sub-second precision. It is deliberately not `|| true`-guarded, so under `set -euo pipefail` a stat/touch failure aborts the seed.

`_assert_delta_newer_than_build_outputs` is a fail-closed post-condition running at the end of `--fresh-checkout` after all mtime-mutating steps: it finds the oldest delta-touched path and the newest `output` under the lane target and aborts unless oldest-delta is strictly newer. An abort yields empty stdout so the caller falls back to a cold rebuild. Ratified as §9.5 inv.12 in docs/prds/warm-lane-pool-cow-seeding.md.

Because the warm-lane seed no longer advances build-output mtimes itself, an mtime inversion today almost always arrived in the cloned base, so every acquire against that generation aborts identically and the pool degrades to cold fallback until the base is re-promoted via `scripts/refresh-warm-base.sh --landed-commit <sha>`. Self-healing by backdating the offending `output` is tracked as task #5632, not done as a drive-by.

For any build script whose correctness matters, prefer content-hash staleness over mtime and republish the watched path's mtime when outputs actually change. Cite the symbols `_touch_git_delta`, `_assert_delta_newer_than_build_outputs`, and the relocation sweep's `find ... -name output -o -name root-output` walk rather than line numbers — the `:745-749` / `:892-898` / `:388-409` coordinates have already drifted.

An architect plan's `files` list is the WRITE-SET: declare only paths the task will CREATE or MODIFY. A file the task merely reads, imports, calls into, or reuses unchanged belongs in the `reuse` section instead.

The architect plan `files` array drives concurrency locks AND the phantom-done / pre-merge gate, which flags any declared file left untouched by the branch commits and forces a narrowing pass via `update_plan_metadata(files=[subset])` followed by `confirm_plan()`; calling `confirm_plan` during a narrowing pass files an escalation.

Task 5334 (δ cluster formation) over-declared crates/reify-eval/src/structural_query.rs defensively, but build_trait_registry, enumerate_descendants, expand_structural_query, apply_trait_filters and apply_cost_aggregation are already `pub(crate)` on main and callable from resolve_order.rs with no visibility widening, so the file was consumed read-only and had to be dropped.

Task 4232 (generic-user-fns γ) reused entity.rs's `check_type_param_bounds` and `satisfies_trait_bound` from entities_phase.rs without editing entity.rs (INV-1: "reused from the structure side, not reinvented"), so entity.rs was over-declared in the plan `files` and had to be dropped during the narrowing pass.

If an architect plan step says "in X.rs (or Y.rs)" or a reuse item says to use a substrate "unchanged", that file is a read-only dependency and must be kept out of `files`. Task 3392 (MITC3+ shell) declared shell_kinematics.rs but only consumed `shell_kinematics::shell_kinematics()` read-only, with the new interior-tying shear helper landing in mitc3_plus.rs.

A new method that calls an existing helper such as `Engine::dispatch_compute_node` in engine_admin.rs must not declare engine_admin.rs in the plan `files`. Nor should a crate root lib.rs be declared to "make the new pub method reachable from integration tests" — inherent `pub fn` methods on an already-`pub struct` are reachable with no re-export.

Reading a shared test harness is not modifying it: task 4738 declared crates/reify-eval/tests/common/differential.rs (a 96 KB shared differential harness) because it pulled it in via `#[path = "common/foo.rs"] mod foo;` and read its constants, but the branch only touched engine_build.rs and the new selective_demand_beta.rs, so differential.rs was dropped.

A task description citing a cfg-gate location such as "gate at crates/reify-eval/build.rs:59-63" (e.g. `has_openvdb`) is almost always a REFERENCE to pre-existing shared build-script infrastructure the task consumes via `#[cfg(has_openvdb)]` attributes, not a directive to modify build.rs; do not declare build.rs unless the gate logic itself changes.

The tree-sitter parser artifacts `tree-sitter-reify/src/{parser.c,grammar.json,node-types.json}` and `src/.grammar_hash.stamp` are gitignored and auto-regenerated from grammar.js by build.rs, so declaring them in a plan's `files` ALWAYS trips the phantom-done gate; for grammar changes declare only grammar.js plus test/corpus and lib.rs.

The counter-pressure to the write-set rule: an architect narrowing pass can only shrink to a SUBSET, so under-declaring is unrecoverable — task 4222 touched crates/reify-eval/src/engine_build.rs (+76 lines) undeclared and could not add it. For in-crate seam work in reify-eval specifically, defensively declaring sibling `engine_*.rs` files may be justified (memory 481fc42f).

In Rust `tracing`, callsite `Interest` is cached PROCESS-GLOBALLY while `tracing::subscriber::with_default` is THREAD-LOCAL, so a test that installs a capturing subscriber and asserts an event fired will FLAKE if any sibling test in the same test binary reaches that callsite first with no subscriber: Interest is cached as `never` and the event is silently dropped.

Measured in reify-eval under task 5075, the tracing Interest cache-poisoning flake failed 6 of 12 runs, with two consecutive identical `cargo test` invocations giving opposite results, and passed in isolation with `-- --exact`. It applies to reify's widespread `CapturingSubscriberBuilder` + `with_default` idiom in engine_purposes.rs, kernel_registry.rs, engine_edit.rs and compute_targets.

Call `reify_test_support::prime_tracing_callsite_cache()` at the top of any reify test that asserts exact tracing event counts via `tracing::subscriber::with_default`; without it a sibling parallel test thread can poison the per-callsite Interest cache to `never`, silently bypassing the per-test subscriber so it captures nothing.

`prime_tracing_callsite_cache` (crates/reify-test-support/src/tracing_support.rs) uses a `std::sync::Once` to install a process-global default `Priming` subscriber whose `register_callsite` returns `Interest::sometimes()`, which disables the static never-cache so `enabled()` is consulted per event; setting the global default also rebuilds the interest cache, repairing callsites already poisoned by an earlier sibling test.

Do NOT fix a tracing Interest cache-poisoning flake with `serial_test`, a global mutex, or `--test-threads=1`, because that couples unrelated tests to a log line; instead assert on a deterministic non-global observable rather than on the tracing event.

Choosing between the two tracing-flake remedies in reify: if the tracing event is genuinely part of the contract under test (a diagnostic that ships, an audited warn count), call `prime_tracing_callsite_cache()`; if the log line is merely the most convenient probe, replace it with a deterministic non-global observable.

reify-test-support offers `CountingSubscriberBuilder` for count-only tracing assertions (registers any subset of {INFO, DEBUG, WARN, ...} plus an optional `target_prefix(...)` filter), while `WarnCapturingSubscriber` is WARN-only and private; for INFO/DEBUG field capture, define a small inline subscriber in the test module mirroring the `MessageVisitor` + `Arc<Mutex<Vec<...>>>` pattern in tracing_support.rs.

`MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` in crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs used to return a single OPEN triangle that `Mesh::validate` rejects under `MeshInvariant::Closed`, silently opting consumers out of the INV-GEO-1 mesh contract. The trap was fixed 2026-07-26 by commit ef4187454d (task #5105 δ).

The historical `MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` mesh was vertices [0,0,0, 1,0,0, 0,1,0] with indices [0,1,2], sitting under an in-source comment that misleadingly called it "a minimal valid mesh". A lone triangle has three boundary edges, so `reify_ir::geometry::Mesh::validate` rejects it with open_edges == 3 — identical to the manifold γ test's `bad_mesh`.

Flipping the tessellate-to-ingest handoff in reify-eval ("site 1", engine_build.rs) to fail-closed enforce broke every test routing MockGeometryKernel through a BRep-to-Mesh conversion (e.g. cross_kernel_handoff.rs), on a contract violation unrelated to what those tests assert — routing, caching, attribute forwarding, and rollback.

The blast radius of the INV-GEO-1 mock trap was bounded: site 1 fires only on CROSS-kernel Mesh handoffs, not on single-kernel tessellate-for-export. Real OCCT tessellations under examples/ and prj/ are valid, so the .ri corpus was expected clean — and was.

The reify mock kernels now hand back `minimal_valid_mesh(with_normals)` — a closed, consistently outward-wound unit tetrahedron with V0=(0,0,0), V1=(1,0,0), V2=(0,1,0), V3=(0,0,1) — the smallest mesh that actually satisfies the mesh contract. The misleading comment was replaced by a doc-comment explaining why a tetrahedron and not a triangle.

When referring to the reify mesh-contract mock, cite the symbol (`minimal_valid_mesh` / `MockGeometryKernel::tessellate` in crates/reify-test-support/src/mocks.rs) rather than a line number — the original entries' `mocks.rs:1794` coordinate had already rotted twice before the canonical merge.

The durable lesson from INV-GEO-1: a canned mock mesh must satisfy `MeshInvariant::Closed`. When a mesh-contract check is made fail-closed on a path fed by a mock, the fix is to emit a closed mesh — not to set the contract mode to warn per-test, which is how the mock hid the problem for months.

An earlier 2026-07-25 note on the INV-GEO-1 mock offered two acceptable fixes — emitting a closed mesh or setting the contract mode to warn per-test — whereas the consolidated record rules out the warn-per-test option as the very mechanism that hid the problem.

Running `reify-audit --pattern PTODO` from a task worktree fails out of the box: the CLI eagerly opens the orchestrator runs.db at startup, defaulting to `data/orchestrator/runs.db`, which is git-untracked and therefore absent in every linked worktree, so it exits 125. Exit 125 is an infrastructure/setup error, not a findings count.

To self-check the PTODO hard gate from a reify task worktree before committing, run `cargo build --release -p reify-audit && ./target/release/reify-audit --pattern PTODO --runs-db "$(mktemp)" --no-jcodemunch --project-root .` — an empty 0-byte file is an acceptable `--runs-db` for PTODO, and `--no-jcodemunch` skips an MCP connection PTODO does not use.
Rebuild reify-audit before a PTODO self-check run: reify embeds sources at build time, so a stale `target/release` binary silently probes yesterday's tree.

The manual reify-audit PTODO run is the only per-task feedback for the PTODO gate: scripts/verify.sh runs the tests/infra run_all.sh pool that owns test_reify_audit_ptodo*.sh only when DF_VERIFY_ROLE=merge, so a per-task verify will NOT catch a bad `#[ignore]` cite.

To activate reify-audit's PTODO liveness lane (which detects `orphaned` cites) from a worktree, set `REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` to the MAIN checkout's `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db`; without it the tool looks for a worktree-relative `./.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.db`, fails, and prints "tasks.db unreachable ... liveness (β) and inverse (ζ) lanes degraded". Keep `--project-root .` so file/git scanning still targets the worktree.

The real PTODO verify gate, tests/infra/test_reify_audit_ptodo.sh, runs `ptodo-baseline-gen` under `env -u REIFY_PTODO_TASKS_DB` (degraded-structural only) and ratchets live structural fingerprints ⊆ the committed empty ptodo-baseline.txt, so liveness-lane `orphaned` findings do NOT block the worktree verify gate — only structural untracked/bare-ignore/malformed-cite do.

PTODO marker keywords are only TODO|FIXME|HACK immediately followed by `(` or `:` (regex `\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b\s*[(:]`), and `RESOLVED(...)` lines are NOT markers; a canonical cite is `#` plus 1 to 5 nonzero digits anywhere on the marker line. Terminal owners (is_terminal_status = done|cancelled) yield `orphaned` findings, while blocked/pending/deferred are LIVE.

This host reaps the Claude session's harness-tracked background tasks roughly hourly, so a long poll that must re-invoke the agent should use the harness Monitor tool rather than a background-Bash watch loop.

Measured 2026-07-22 on the reify host: plain background-Bash watch loops (run_in_background curl-poll loops) were reaped within the hour, with two consecutive watchers dying as 'stopped', while the harness Monitor tool survived full 1-hour windows repeatedly.

For a helper loop that does not need to notify the agent, run it setsid-detached (`setsid nohup script > log 2>&1 </dev/null &`) so it survives the hourly sweeps; give it a self-terminate guard that greps the watcher-<project> lease file for its own slug each cycle, a MAX_CYCLES backstop, and a per-cycle status file the agent can poll.

Background-task reaping on this host is load-correlated rather than deterministic: under merge-verify CPU saturation, background tasks and even `setsid nohup`-detached children were swept within ~1-2 minutes, while under light load the same polls survived their full 10-20 minute cap.

Simulating a nextest-less host for reify's tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh suites splits into two different problems: making scripts/verify.sh itself genuinely take its NEXTEST=0 fallback (hide cargo-nextest properly), versus changing only what a suite believes (sed a temp copy of the suite).

scripts/verify.sh's cargo-nextest probe deliberately disambiguates "genuinely absent" from "present but probe failing": if `cargo nextest --version` fails but `command -v cargo-nextest` still resolves, verify.sh hard-fails after retries instead of falling back to the cargo-test plan.

Making cargo-nextest appear genuinely absent to scripts/verify.sh needs BOTH a stubbed `cargo` on PATH AND an empty temp $HOME with a restricted PATH excluding `~/.cargo/bin` — a stub alone is insufficient because `apply_env()` re-sources `~/.cargo/env` and re-prepends the real bin dir. The WORKDIR/SHIM_DIR/TMP_HOME idiom lives in tests/infra/test_verify_nextest_probe.sh (task 4971).

For `--scope all --print-plan` alone, an exit-1-for-all `cargo` stub suffices on its own to simulate a nextest-less host (no non-nextest cargo call is made), so the empty-HOME/restricted-PATH rig is only required once a fixture goes past plan-printing into an actual nextest-vs-test execution branch.

When a tests/infra plan-oracle suite needs other tools from `~/.cargo/bin` (task 5599), simulate a nextest-less host with a symlink farm mirroring `~/.cargo/bin` MINUS cargo-nextest, prepended to the real PATH with the real `~/.cargo/bin` element filtered out, plus HOME=<tempdir>. CARGO_HOME must NOT be exported to the real `~/.cargo`, or cargo re-resolves cargo-nextest from `$CARGO_HOME/bin` and the plan flips back to nextest=1.

The naive nextest-hiding recipe `PATH="$STUB:/usr/bin:/bin"` strips `~/.cargo/bin` wholesale, which also removes the tree-sitter CLI and makes tests/infra/test_verify_semaphore_e2e.sh's suite-start `ensure_tree_sitter_ready` gate fail 5 execute-mode sections (A/B/C/F1/H) for reasons unrelated to nextest.

To change what a tests/infra/test_verify_*.sh suite believes about nextest without touching host env, sed a TEMP COPY of the suite: pin `SCRIPT_DIR` to `$PWD/tests/infra` so the copy still sources test_helpers.sh, rewrite `*"nextest=1"*)` to a never-matching pattern so nextest-gated asserts SKIP, and rewrite `cargo nextest run ` to `cargo nextest-SIM run ` so plan-line greps are unmatchable.

Do not simulate a nextest-less host by copying a patched scripts/verify.sh: verify.sh and the tests/infra suites both derive REPO_ROOT from their own BASH_SOURCE dir, which forces scratch files into scripts/ and tests/infra/ where run_all.sh may pick them up.

An architect re-invoked on a task/NNNN branch can find its committed TDD work intact while `.task/plan.json` is lost or desynced; the correct recovery is to reconstruct a faithful plan.json mirroring the committed steps rather than redo the work.

`.task/plan.json` is gitignored and filesystem-only, so it never survives a warm-lane re-seed, while the branch's committed TDD step commits (`test(NNNN): step-K RED` / `feat(NNNN): step-K GREEN`, sometimes prereq tags like `pre-1`) survive intact on task/NNNN.
On any architect re-invocation the first two commands are `git log --oneline main..HEAD` and `ls -la .task/`; if `.task/plan.json` does exist, then check whether its steps are actually marked.

Four trigger signatures for warm-lane plan.json loss: task metadata `reblock_guard` reading like 'warm-lane acquire fault for branch NNNN (seed/worktree...)'; an architect finding branch commits but no plan.json; a branch annotated 'RESUME CONTEXT: this is a re-queue'; or a requeued task surfaced with a different task's plan.json attached.

A fifth signature is desync rather than loss: `.task/plan.json` is present and structurally correct but entirely unmarked (every prerequisite and step at status=pending, commit=null) while `git log main..HEAD` shows the work committed, because the implementer died after committing but before its first `mark_step_done`. Recovery is identical.

To recover a lost plan.json, map each commit to its step by touched files using `git log --oneline main..HEAD` plus per-commit `--stat`/diff, then call `confirm_plan()` and `mark_step_done` per commit, letting the executor re-verify the already-GREEN steps rather than redoing them.

Do not call `report_task_already_done` for work that lives only on a task branch: that path requires the commit be reachable from main. The concrete check is `git ls-tree main -- <path>` — a branch-only commit does not qualify.

If the commits on a resumed task branch implement only part of the task, plan only the remaining gap and do not re-plan already-green RED tests, but still list the full task footprint in `create_plan` `files[]` so locks and the phantom-done check see all branch-vs-base diffs. Seen on task 5031 (gui-state-sync L2).

On task 5357 the `.task/plan.json` was a dangling symlink whose target `worktrees/.task-meta/<lane>/plan.json` was missing; the architect derived the steps from `git diff main...HEAD`, called confirm_plan, then filed `escalate_info(category='infra_issue')` noting the metadata loss.

A `chore: save WIP before rebase` commit on a resumed task branch can contain a real step's full implementation rather than noise, so run `git show --stat` or `git show` on every WIP-labeled commit before dismissing it (observed on task 4168).

The reify-gui debug MCP has a set of known gotchas that produce a CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER rather than an error; each has already caused at least one false conclusion in a real session. This gotcha appendix is the companion to topic=reify-debug-mcp-driving, which covers the port contract, transport, and launch recipes.

The reify-gui debug MCP's `wait_for_idle` does not mean settled: it returned `idle_after_ms ~= 28` for bottom_deck_split.ri while async tessellation and geometry-query passes were still running, and the process SIGSEGV'd ~6 s later. After wait_for_idle, confirm via `engine_state` values AND process aliveness.

`engine_state.values` in the reify-gui debug MCP is a LIST of `{id, value}` dicts, not a dict. A `.get('mass')` extraction therefore silently reads None and manufactures a "mass is missing" result — this produced a false alarm in-session. Index by scanning for the matching `id`.

`mesh_stats` and `engine_state.meshes` UNDER-REPORT large composed scenes in reify-gui (bug filed 2026-07-22). For completeness questions, screenshots are ground truth; mesh_stats remains fine for "which entity_paths emitted a mesh", just not for "is everything here".
Reify-gui debug MCP responses are nested JSON twice: `result.content[0].text` is itself a JSON string needing a second parse. Forgetting this yields a string where you expected an object.

A detached `setsid` launch of reify-gui has no shell, so a native signal death prints nothing and the captured stderr log is simply EMPTY. Silence plus a missing process means a native signal, not a clean exit; use a wrapper that echoes `$?` to a log for the exact signal (139 = SEGV, 134 = ABRT, 137 = OOM-kill).

To capture a reify-gui native crash, run `gdb -batch -ex "set pagination off" -ex "handle SIG33 SIG34 SIGPWR SIGXCPU nostop noprint pass" -ex run -ex "thread apply all bt 12" --args target/debug/reify-gui <file.ri>` with REIFY_DEBUG=1 and REIFY_DEBUG_PORT set, then trigger via MCP `open_file` — the MCP stays reachable under gdb with ~5 s startup lag.

The reify-gui stack-overflow signature is a SIGSEGV at a function's ENTRY line with reference arguments reading 0x0, in deep recursion on a "tokio-rt-worker" thread (2 MB stack) — that is the guard-page stack probe, not a null dereference. Reproducing the same input through the CLI proves only that the main thread's 8 MB stack was enough.

reify-gui has TWO distinct MCP dispatch systems: `mcp_context.rs::mcp_tool_call_impl` handles engine-locked `reify_*` tools (tested in tests/mcp_dispatch_tests.rs), while `debug_server.rs::dispatch_tool` handles the `/mcp` debug tools and its default arm delegates frontend-mediated tools to `DebugBridge::query_frontend` in debug.rs.

reify-gui's DebugBridge::query_frontend emits a `debug-request` Tauri event and awaits a oneshot keyed by id, completed by `DebugBridge::resolve(id, json)` when gui/src/debug/bridge.ts invokes `debug_response`. Unit-testing that round-trip needs `tauri::test::mock_app()` (MockRuntime), which requires DebugBridge to be generic over `R: Runtime` (it pinned `AppHandle<Wry>`) and the tauri `test` feature enabled.

`pkill -f <pattern>` and `pgrep -f <pattern>` match the FULL command line of every process, including the shell running your own command, whose command line literally contains the pattern — so never match processes by a pattern your own command line contains.

Kill self-match was observed with `pkill -f phase0-run.sh`, `pkill -f load-sampler.sh` and `pkill -f 'cargo build --workspace'`, each killing the issuing shell (exit 144 = 128+SIGTERM, or "Killed" mid-output). `kill -TERM -<PGID>` is the same trap when the PGID is shared with the Bash tool's subshell.

When a pkill self-match kills the issuing shell in a compound command, everything after the pkill never runs — but the intended targets usually still died correctly and persisted log files survive, so re-read them in a follow-up command.

Check self-match is the sneakier failure mode: `pgrep -f "cargo build -p reify-cli"` used as a liveness probe reports "still running" forever because the checking shell's own command line matches. It cost ~40 min of wasted wall-clock on 2026-07-25 on a build that had finished in 2m35s, and an `until pgrep ...` watcher loop matches itself and never exits.

Instead of killing by pattern, resolve the PID first (via `ps`, `ss -p`, or `pgrep` read into a variable) and then `kill <pid>`. If a pattern is unavoidable, pick one that cannot appear in your own command line, such as the target lane's absolute `target/` dir path.

For liveness probes, the bracket trick `pgrep -f 'carg[o] build'` matches the target but not the literal text in your own argv, and `pgrep -x cargo` scoped by cwd avoids full-command-line matching entirely. Better still, grep the build log for `Finished`/`error` or test the target binary's mtime instead of process-matching.

In the warm-lane sandbox `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f` match command lines system-wide across all worktrees and lanes, so a match may belong to an unrelated `_merge-*` lane's in-flight verify. Check `readlink -f /proc/<pid>/cwd` before treating any match as yours; this scope trap is tracked as separate entry 7b8da91e.

Multi-statement Bash tool commands occasionally get mangled by the harness's eval-wrapper collapsing newlines between statements (observed: an invalid `tail -8`, echoes concatenated). Prefer one logical command per call or `&&` chains, and write `tail -n N`, not `tail -N`.

In the reify compiler, whether a `Boolean{left,right}` operand carries a `GeomRef::Sub` consumption edge depends on the OPERAND'S SHAPE: cross-sub `self.<sub>.<member>` operands do, while bare idents naming a sibling geometry-let and function calls do not.

In `resolve_boolean_arg` (crates/reify-compiler/src/geometry_boolean.rs), a `self.<sub>.<member>` operand hits the task-3441 cross-sub pre-check, which calls `try_resolve_cross_sub_geom_ref` and returns `Some((GeomRef::Sub(...), vec![]))` — a real Sub consumption edge with zero sub-ops accumulated; eval then seeds `named_steps["<sub>.<member>"]`.

Boolean operands go through `resolve_boolean_arg`, which has no bare-Ident pre-check and INLINES the operand's initializer as sub-ops referenced by `GeomRef::Step(n)`. Measured: for `param geometry = difference(body, holes)` the names "body" and "holes" appear nowhere in the compiled realization's operations, so `extract_realization_edges` is NOT a complete oracle for which sibling realizations are consumed downstream.

The private `extract_realization_edges` in crates/reify-eval/src/deps.rs is characterized as the authoritative enumeration of which `CompiledGeometryOp` variants carry consumption edges — Boolean{left,right}, Modify|Transform|Pattern{target}, Sweep{profiles}, Isosurface{grid} — with `GeomRef::Step(_)` skipped as intra-node and Primitive/Curve/Profile carrying none.

Inside `RealizationDecl.operations`, a bare `GeomRef::Sub` name (0 dots) means a same-structure sibling and a dotted name ("sub.member") means cross-sub — a namespace split safe by construction because reify DSL identifiers never contain '.'. `extract_realization_edges` is not re-exported through `pub mod deps`, so consumers outside reify-eval (e.g. gui/src-tauri) must mirror its match arms rather than call it.

The complete name-level source for sibling geometry references in reify is the value-cell layer: `TopologyTemplate.value_cells[*].default_expr` carries `ValueRef(ValueCellId{entity, member})` for every sibling reference. Caveat: a `: Rigid` structure's auto-derived mass/centroid/moment_of_inertia lets also hold `ValueRef(geometry)`, so a consumption scan must count only Geometry-typed cells as consumers.

Adding a frontend-mediated tool to the reify-debug MCP needs only two touch points: a `ToolDef` entry in `tool_defs()` in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs, and a handler in the `buildHandlers(ctx)` map in gui/src/debug/bridge.ts. No new Rust dispatch match-arm is required.

`dispatch_tool`'s default arm in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs — `_ => state.debug_bridge.query_frontend(name, params).await` — forwards any unmatched tool name to the JS bridge, so a bridge-only handler such as `focus_editor` works via `tools/call` without rebuilding the Tauri binary.

The reify debug-MCP tool registry lives in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs (`tool_defs()` and `dispatch_tool(state, name, params)`), NOT in gui/src-tauri/src/debug.rs, despite PRDs GR-016 §2.3 and mesh-morphing.md calling it "the debug.rs registry". debug.rs houses the unrelated `DebugBridge` for frontend-mediated oneshot RPCs, and there is no gui/src-tauri/src/debug_bridge.rs at all (confirmed absent 2026-07-27).

State-bound reify-debug MCP tools that touch the engine or disk — engine_state, mesh_stats, open_file, wait_for_idle, load_fixture, and the stateless morph stats — do get an explicit Rust dispatch arm, via the `run_on_engine` helper in gui/src-tauri/src/debug_server.rs.

Image-returning reify-debug MCP tools (screenshot, screenshot_window, element_screenshot) must also be listed in `is_image_tool()`, or `tools/call` will not strip the data-URL prefix and emit an MCP image content block.

Frontend store fields read by a reify-debug bridge handler must be added to the `DebugStores` type in gui/src/debug/types.ts, which exposes only a structural subset of the real engineStore (it lacked compileDiagnostics/tessellationDiagnostics until task 4297). A field missing there is a silent read failure, not a Rust compile error.

For a frontend-mediated reify-debug tool the Rust-side test just asserts the tool_defs schema (object type, required fields), with precedents in debug_server.rs's own test module such as tool_defs_includes_set_camera and is_image_tool_recognizes_both_screenshot_variants. Frontend bridge unit tests go in gui/src/__tests__/debugBridge.test.tsx — the .TSX extension, not the .ts that task metadata `files` lists sometimes claim.

jsdom has no layout engine, so `getBoundingClientRect()` returns width 0 under vitest; a reify-debug bridge handler needing visibility must use CSS visibility instead, which is why the `ui_outline` handler does.

gui/src/__tests__/debugParity.test.ts is the executable contract for the reify-debug tool registry: it regex-extracts `ToolDef { name: "..." }` from the Rust source and checks frontend/Rust parity. Where prose and that test disagree, the test wins.

Line numbers in debug_server.rs rot — cite symbols instead. Retired entries pinned dispatch_tool's default arm at "~:481"; as of 2026-07-27 it is at :1069, with tool_defs at :35, is_image_tool at :1030, dispatch_tool at :1047 and run_on_engine at :1077.
